domain_label: Turlock Independent Automotive Supply Chain, Capex, Labor, Licensing and Operating Model
purpose: A session-bounded method for an independent Turlock automotive-service operator to design and harden the operating model of a shop across the seven cataloged sub-categories (collision, detailing, mechanical repair, parts retail, smog/inspection, tires/wheels, transmission), by pinning the sub-category's dominant input and cost center, mapping the parts/paint/tire/rebuild-kit supplier universe verified to serve the Turlock/Modesto Central Valley geography, sizing the equipment and capex ladder from a $5k mobile detailing rig to a $50k-$150k+ collision booth-and-frame setup, choosing the owner-operator versus W-2-crew versus credential-gated labor model, clearing the BAR ARD / STAR / smog-technician / DRP / air-district licensing gates before taking in work, and labeling every revenue, margin and capex figure as a benchmark estimate rather than a stated fact for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business operating dataset is supplied; channel mixes, capex bands, labor models and cost-share weights are reasoned heuristic priors keyed to the automotive deep-dive, not invoices or filings

the operator runs one of the 19 cataloged independent Turlock automotive formats profiled in the deep-dive (collision, detailing, mechanical repair, parts retail, smog test-only or test-and-repair, tires/wheels, transmission)

the geography is Turlock / Stanislaus County in the Modesto MSA, ~15 miles south of Modesto, inside a dense dairy/nut/food-processing ag belt with an aging high-mileage fleet-heavy vehicle parc, in 2026

supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts, unless the deep-dive cites the relationship; bay counts, headcount and throughput are UNKNOWN for every named firm

per-business dollar revenue is never asserted; any dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate (national per-unit benchmark x an inferred size signal x sub-category band) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
the operator holds or is obtaining the required BAR Automotive Repair Dealer registration and any sub-category station/technician license before taking in work for compensation
exclusions: per-business revenue, profit, bay count, or throughput stated as fact (only labeled benchmark estimates and cited public fee/benchmark figures are used)
estimating ad-spend, marketing channels, and customer-acquisition strategy beyond noting the Spanish-language and heritage referral channel as a labor/demand input
site selection, lease negotiation, and the buildout/real-estate financing decision beyond the equipment-and-capex sourcing node
saturation, white-space, and competitive-structure strategy (covered by the market-saturation KB)
wage-band setting and hiring sourcing beyond naming the owner-operator, W-2-crew, and credential-gated labor models and their capacity constraint
EV powertrain-service strategy beyond flagging it as a demand-erosion risk to the smog and transmission lanes

competency_questions.question: For this specific Turlock automotive sub-category, what is the dominant input and cost center, and which inputs or cost lines must the operating plan protect first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUBCATEGORY_COST_PROFILE names the sub-category's dominant cost center from the deep-dive (marinated labor and paint for collision, chemicals/coatings for detailing, billed technician labor and parts for mechanical, shelf inventory for parts retail, the analyzer and certificate for smog, tire COGS and attached service for tires, rebuild kits and skilled labor for transmission) and ranks the remaining cost lines by share and risk

competency_questions.question: What is the realistic supplier universe verified to serve Turlock/Modesto/Central Valley, and how is it segmented by sub-category channel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLIER_UNIVERSE enumerates the paint/jobber, aftermarket-parts, tire-wholesaler, rebuild-kit, smog-analyzer, buying-group, and local Turlock Auto Parts nodes named in the deep-dive and tags each as verified-to-serve vs representative inference

competency_questions.question: How should the operator choose the inventory and ordering model, and what drives JIT per-job ordering versus shelf-stock carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INVENTORY_MODEL contrasts the JIT per-repair-order service-shop model against the inventory-carry parts-retail model and gives a sub-category rule for shelf depth versus same-day jobber pulls

competency_questions.question: When does same-day local jobber and buying-group sourcing beat OE-dealer or direct-distributor sourcing, and vice versa?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JOBBER_PARTS_SUPPLY and BUYING_GROUP_LEVERAGE contrast multiple same-day jobber deliveries and member rebates against OE special-order lead time and price, and give a routing rule by part type and urgency

competency_questions.question: How does the operator size the equipment and capex ladder for the chosen sub-category, from a mobile detailing rig to a collision booth and frame?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAPEX_EQUIPMENT_LADDER places the sub-category on the deep-dive ladder (mobile detailing $5k-$15k, fixed detailing/per-bay mechanical mid-five-figures to $50k-$150k, smog analyzer single-instrument capex, collision booth+frame $50k-$150k+) and names the capital anchor

competency_questions.question: How is collision paint, panel, and equipment supply set up, and why is DRP gatekeeping the binding constraint, not accident volume?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COLLISION_PAINT_PARTS routes PPG/Axalta paint via LKQ Refinish and aftermarket/recycled panels via LKQ and OE via Worldpac, and COLLISION_BOOTH_FRAME plus DRP_GATE explain the booth/frame capex and insurer-relationship gate that caps the count at two

competency_questions.question: How is tire and wheel supply sourced and why must independents survive on attached service rather than tire-product margin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIRE_WHEEL_SUPPLY routes American Tire Distributors/NTW and direct-from-manufacturer tire supply, states the thin tire-resale margin, and explains the service-attach (alignment/brake/mechanical) survival mechanism the deep-dive documents

competency_questions.question: How is the smog/inspection station set up, and how does the regulated $8.25 certificate fee differ from the unregulated test price?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SMOG_STATION_LICENSING states the BAR station license, STAR certification, and licensed-inspector requirement, cites the regulated $8.25 certificate fee as the only regulated dollar figure, and treats the $30-$80 test price as an unregulated market estimate

competency_questions.question: How is transmission rebuild-kit and drivetrain-parts supply set up for the high-ticket low-volume specialty format?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSMISSION_KIT_SUPPLY routes Transtar/NexaMotion soft-parts and master rebuild kits, torque converters, and Transend recycled units, and matches the per-job JIT kit-ordering cadence to the high-average-repair-order low-volume reality

competency_questions.question: Which labor model fits the sub-category, and where is credential-gated labor a hiring bottleneck rather than just a cost line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABOR_MODEL distinguishes owner-operator/family-run (Nona's, Mando's, Balswick's), W-2 technician crews, and the solo mobile-detailer analog, and flags licensed smog inspectors and I-CAR/ASE collision techs as credential-constrained labor

competency_questions.question: What licensing, registration, and environmental gates bind a shop before it can take in work for compensation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_GATES cites the BAR ARD registration, the CDTFA resale/seller's permit, the smog station/technician and STAR forks, the air-district paint-booth VOC permit and hazmat handling, and the city business license, and ranks which sub-categories each binds

competency_questions.question: How is revenue, margin, and capex modeled honestly without asserting any named business's actual figures, and how is a benchmark estimate labeled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINANCIAL_HONESTY_CHARTER derives every figure as a labeled benchmark estimate (national per-unit benchmark x an inferred size signal x sub-category band) tagged estimate-not-actual with method, public source, and confidence, separates the regulated $8.25 fee fact from the $30-$80 market estimate, and names a confirmation path

glossary.definition: The California Bureau of Automotive Repair registration any business performing tests, repairs, or diagnosis for compensation must hold and renew; it binds nearly every Turlock auto sub-category except pure detailing, and is the first gate cleared before taking in work.

A voluntary BAR smog-station certification that lets a station inspect DMV-directed vehicles; it carries no application or renewal fee but requires meeting performance standards plus a current ARD and station license, and losing it removes directed-vehicle volume (All Valley Smog and Speed Pass Smog are STAR).

The state-set $8.25 per-certificate fee, the only genuinely regulated dollar figure in the Turlock auto sector; the widely quoted $30-$80 per-test price is an unregulated competitive market band and is labeled an estimate, never a regulated fact.

An insurer's referral arrangement that drives roughly 90% of collision revenue; landing DRP relationships, not finding accident volume, is the binding constraint on a Turlock body shop, which is why the collision count is structurally capped at two.

A local parts wholesaler (NAPA, O'Reilly, WORLDPAC, plus local Turlock Auto Parts) that makes multiple same-day deliveries to a repair shop, enabling the JIT per-repair-order model that keeps shelf inventory minimal beyond fast movers.

A parts buying cooperative (Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Federated, National Pronto / 'The Group', ~5,000 locations and ~$7B member revenue) that gives an independent parts store or repair shop rebate-and-price leverage it cannot earn alone against the national jobbers.

A Transtar (NexaMotion Group) soft-parts, master, or super rebuild kit plus torque converters and valve bodies shipped per transmission job (often 1-3 days), the JIT input that defines the high-average-repair-order low-volume transmission economics; Transend supplies recycled units.

The survival mechanism for independent tire shops, who lose the commodity tire-product lane to chains and online and instead profit from bundling alignment, brake, and general mechanical work onto the tire sale (E&M sells parts/tires; Balswick's does tires plus repair plus detail).

The spray booth, frame/measuring system, mixing bank, and welders that make collision the heaviest-capex sub-category, commonly $50k-$150k+ (labeled estimate, wide range); together with air-district VOC permits and DRP gatekeeping it caps the local body-shop count.

A revenue, margin, or capex figure built as a published national per-unit benchmark (per bay / per truck / per station / per car) times an inferred size signal (years in business, bay count read from the offering, mobile-vs-shop, DRP language) times the sub-category band, explicitly tagged estimate-not-actual with a method, a public source, and a confidence level, never a claim of a named business's actual figure.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for Turlock/Central Valley automotive supply-chain, capex, labor, and licensing work units, grounded in the automotive sector deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md sec 3-4 and 6, businesses.json, count=19): its named supplier universe (PPG/Axalta paint via LKQ Refinish, LKQ/Worldpac parts, NAPA/O'Reilly/WORLDPAC jobbers, American Tire Distributors/NTW, Transtar/NexaMotion rebuild kits, the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance/Federated/Pronto buying groups, BAR-approved EIS/OIS smog-analyzer vendors), its per-sub-category cost centers and capex ladder, its published cost-structure benchmarks, and its BAR ARD / STAR / smog-technician / DRP / air-district licensing fee facts; no supplied operating dataset
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Turlock Automotive Sector Deep-Dive (FACTORY/turlock_business/analysis/automotive/DEEPDIVE.md sec 3-4, 6; businesses.json count=19); CA Bureau of Automotive Repair (bar.ca.gov licensing-ard, smog, STAR FAQ; $8.25 certificate fee, ~$20 inspector app/renewal); paint via PPG/Axalta and LKQ Refinish; aftermarket/recycled parts via LKQ and OE via Worldpac; mechanical jobbers NAPA/O'Reilly/WORLDPAC plus local Turlock Auto Parts; buying groups Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance/Federated/National Pronto (~5,000 locations, ~$7B member revenue); tire wholesalers American Tire Distributors (90k+ SKUs)/NTW; transmission rebuild kits Transtar (NexaMotion Group)/Transend; PartsTech/IBISWorld/Statista revenue and density benchmarks; financialmodelslab/StartCosts/Kleen-Rite capex bands; U.S. Census/DataUSA demographics; heuristic priors where no operating dataset is supplied

nodes.definition: Pin the demand driver that bounds every operating decision in this sector: Turlock auto-service demand keys to the vehicle parc, not households, so the immediate base of roughly 45,000-50,000 registered vehicles (estimate) across ~72,500 residents, skewed toward an aging high-mileage ag/fleet-heavy parc in a dairy/nut/food-processing belt, over-indexes the town on essential mechanical, tire, smog, and transmission work. CSU Stanislaus and a ~46% Hispanic/Latino base drive older cash-pay vehicles rather than warranty dealer service. This parc read, with its directional A/C-summer and pre-winter-tire seasonality, is the raw demand input that sizes capacity and the labor model downstream.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the vehicle parc size, age, or fleet mix materially shifts

pros.claim: Keying demand to the vehicle parc rather than households tells the operator which sub-categories are essential and demand-resilient
pros.example: an ag-belt parc of high-mileage farm trucks over-indexing the town on mechanical, tire, and transmission work a richer newer-car suburb would not need

cons.claim: A parc-level read masks sub-category swings like the EV transition that erode smog and transmission demand unevenly
cons.example: treating the parc as uniform while BEV adoption quietly removes smog-eligible and multi-speed-transmission vehicles

failure_modes: sizing capacity to population instead of the vehicle parc
ignoring the ag-fleet over-index that keeps essential lanes denser than a generic town
acceptance_tests: the parc-size estimate and the aging/ag-fleet/cash-pay skew are stated with the sub-categories they make essential, distinguished from chain-owned commodity lanes
revisit_triggers: a material shift in the local vehicle parc size, age, or fleet mix
the EV transition measurably erodes a smog or transmission demand pool

nodes.definition: Ground the operating model in the 19 cataloged independent Turlock automotive firms across seven sub-categories: collision (Broadway Auto & AutoBody Repair, Complete Collision Works), detailing (2 Guys, Adrian's, Cen-Cal, Turlock Auto Detailing Co., Veras), mechanical (E & M Auto Service and Parts, Nona's Auto Center, Turlock Auto Service), parts retail (Turlock Auto Parts), smog (All Valley Smog, Speed Pass Smog, Turlock Quick Smog & Repair), tires (Balswick's since 1945, Countryside Tire & Brake, Mando's Tires and Wheels), transmission (Al's Transmissions, Turlock Transmissions). Heavy cross-categorization means functional mechanical capacity exceeds the headline three, and this catalog is the coverage floor every supplier and capex node is matched against.

excluded: chains, dealers, and the informal/mobile tail
asserting any firm's bay count or revenue

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the cataloged independent set or a firm's sub-category changes

pros.claim: Anchoring on the named catalog keeps every supplier and capex match grounded in real independents rather than abstractions
pros.example: reading E&M's secondary tires-and-parts categories as a mini-integrated mechanical shop when matching its jobber and tire supply

cons.claim: The catalog is a floor that excludes the informal/mobile tail and the chains, so it understates true local capacity
cons.example: treating the three primary mechanical shops as total capacity when tire and smog cross-sellers add functional bays

failure_modes: counting primary categories as total capacity and missing cross-sellers
treating the catalog as a ceiling rather than an identifiable-independent floor
acceptance_tests: the 19 firms are listed by primary sub-category with cross-categorization noted, and the catalog is labeled a coverage floor not a ceiling
revisit_triggers: a cataloged firm opens, closes, merges, or changes sub-category
a new identifiable independent enters the catalog

nodes.definition: Establish the tiered licensing footprint that gates any auto shop before it takes in work for compensation: the BAR Automotive Repair Dealer (ARD) registration binding nearly every sub-category except pure detailing, the CDTFA resale/seller's permit for any shop reselling parts or tires, the smog station-and-technician license with its STAR fork, the air-district paint-booth VOC permit and hazmat handling for used oil/solvents/ATF/tires (heaviest on collision), and the City of Turlock business license. The tiering explains the count: detailing clears no BAR gate (count five), collision faces ARD plus de-facto I-CAR/ASE plus booth permits plus DRP (count two). Auto repair is governed by BAR, not the CSLB.

included: BAR ARD, CDTFA permit, smog/STAR, air-district VOC, hazmat, city license
excluded: the DRP relationship gate (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a BAR, STAR, CDTFA, air-district, or city licensing requirement changes

pros.claim: Pricing the tiered licensing gate up front prevents a shop from taking in work it cannot legally perform for compensation
pros.example: a would-be smog station confirming its BAR station license, technician license, and STAR standing before advertising directed-vehicle inspections

cons.claim: Treating every gate as fixed over-states the entry wall for a pure detailing operation that clears no BAR gate at all
cons.example: a mobile detailer assuming an ARD registration applies when detailing needs none

failure_modes: taking in repair work without an ARD registration
missing the air-district VOC paint-booth permit a collision shop must hold
acceptance_tests: the ARD, CDTFA, smog/STAR, air-district VOC, hazmat, and city-license requirements are listed with the sub-categories each binds before any work is taken in
revisit_triggers: a BAR, STAR, CDTFA, air-district, or city fee or rule changes
the operator adds a sub-category that crosses a new gate

nodes.definition: Bind the operating model to the deep-dive's financial-honesty charter: per-business dollar revenue is not public for these privately held independents and is never stated as an actual figure for any named firm. Every revenue, margin, market-size, and capex figure is a labeled benchmark estimate carrying the word estimate, a method, a public source basis, and a confidence band. The one regulated dollar fact is the $8.25 state smog certificate fee; the $30-$80 per-test price is a market estimate, never a regulated fact. Structural facts (suppliers serving the geography, licensing regimes, state-set fees, demographics) are cited fact; supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference; coverage of 19 is a floor.

excluded: the estimate-derivation method itself (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a public fee/benchmark updates or actual financial data becomes available

pros.claim: A binding honesty charter keeps every dollar figure a disciplined estimate that never libels or misrepresents a private business
pros.example: stating a collision shop's revenue only as a benchmark x inferred-bay-count band tagged estimate-not-actual, never as a reported figure

cons.claim: Strict labeling adds friction and can read as hedging when a downstream reader wants a single point figure
cons.example: a planner frustrated that no node states a flat dollar number for a named shop

failure_modes: stating a per-business dollar figure as fact instead of a labeled estimate
presenting the $30-$80 test price as a regulated fact like the $8.25 fee
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure is labeled estimate-not-actual with method/source/confidence, and the $8.25 certificate fee is the only figure stated as a regulated fact
revisit_triggers: a public fee or benchmark updates
actual invoice or filing data becomes available to replace an estimate

nodes.definition: Enumerate the realistic supplier universe verified to serve Turlock/Modesto/Central Valley and segment it by channel: collision paint (PPG, Axalta via PBE jobbers and LKQ Refinish) and panels (LKQ aftermarket/recycled, Worldpac OE); mechanical jobbers (NAPA, O'Reilly, WORLDPAC) plus local Turlock Auto Parts; tire wholesalers (American Tire Distributors with 90k+ SKUs, NTW, direct from Michelin/Goodyear); transmission rebuild kits (Transtar/NexaMotion, Transend recycled); BAR-approved EIS/OIS smog-analyzer vendors; and the parts buying groups (Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance, Federated, National Pronto). Each node is tagged verified-to-serve-this-geography versus representative inference, because supplier-to-named-business links are inference unless the deep-dive cites them.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the verified supplier set or its Turlock delivery reach changes

pros.claim: A pre-mapped geography-verified supplier list stops the operator from chasing vendors who do not serve the county
pros.example: knowing ATD and Transtar already serve the Central Valley avoids sourcing through a distant distributor with an excluding minimum

cons.claim: A fixed universe can ossify and miss a new entrant or a vendor that recently extended delivery into the county
cons.example: overlooking a newly opened regional PBE jobber because it postdates the deep-dive snapshot

failure_modes: treating an inferred supplier link as a confirmed contract
omitting the local Turlock Auto Parts node that mechanical shops lean on for hot-shot pulls
acceptance_tests: the universe lists at least six channel segments with at least one named geography-verified provider each, and tags every named-business link verified or inference
revisit_triggers: a supplier opens, closes, merges, or changes its Turlock delivery reach
a buying group or wholesaler restructures its Central Valley coverage

nodes.definition: Pin, for the operator's specific sub-category, the dominant cost center the deep-dive marks and how the remaining cost lines rank by share and risk: billed technician labor (50-75% labor margin) plus parts (20-30% margin, ~30-40% of revenue) for mechanical, paint-and-panel plus DRP-compressed labor for collision, drum-bought chemicals and high-margin ceramic coatings for detailing, shelf inventory carry for parts retail, the analyzer plus the $8.25 certificate and labor for smog, thin tire COGS offset by attached service for tires, and rebuild kits plus skilled labor for high-ARO transmission. This profile is the raw input that bounds every supplier, capex, and labor choice downstream.

included: cost-line ranking by share and risk
the cost lines the plan must protect first

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the sub-category, service mix, or dominant cost center changes

pros.claim: Naming the one dominant cost center focuses operating effort where margin is actually won or lost
pros.example: a mechanical shop recognizing billed technician labor as its engine and prioritizing technician productivity over chasing cheaper parts

cons.claim: Over-fixating on the biggest cost line can starve attention from a smaller line with higher stockout or compliance risk
cons.example: a collision shop optimizing paint cost while letting a back-ordered OE panel stall a whole repair order

failure_modes: importing another sub-category's cost profile so the wrong cost line is protected
treating a labor-driven shop as a parts-cost problem when billed-hours productivity dominates
acceptance_tests: the profile names the sub-category's dominant cost center as the deep-dive marks it and ranks at least three more cost lines by share and risk
revisit_triggers: the operator changes or adds a sub-category or service line
a previously minor cost line becomes the binding cost or risk

nodes.definition: Decide the inventory and ordering model for the sub-category, the structural fork that separates the two capital models coexisting in this sector. The JIT service shops (mechanical, collision, transmission, tires) order parts per repair order and hold minimal shelf stock beyond fast movers, tying capital up in equipment and labor; the single parts retailer ties capital up in broad shelf inventory and POS/catalog systems. The choice is driven by whether the operator sells parts off the shelf or consumes them per job, by jobber same-day delivery density, and by the buying-group depth that makes inventory carry viable. The output is a target inventory posture per part class.

included: fast-mover stock vs same-day jobber pulls
excluded: the specific jobber or buying-group terms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: jobber delivery density, buying-group terms, or the part-class mix changes

pros.claim: Choosing JIT per repair order keeps a service shop's capital in revenue-earning equipment and labor rather than dead shelf stock
pros.example: a mechanical shop holding only fast movers and pulling everything else same-day from NAPA/O'Reilly/WORLDPAC

cons.claim: JIT exposes the shop to a same-day delivery gap or an OE back-order that a shelf-stocked part would have covered
cons.example: a transmission rebuild stalling on a 1-3 day kit back-order with no spare on hand

failure_modes: running an inventory-carry model against the nationals without a trade-account base
stocking slow-moving parts that tie up capital a JIT shop needs for tooling
acceptance_tests: the inventory posture is set per part class as JIT same-day or shelf-carry, with the capital-model rationale stated for the sub-category
revisit_triggers: jobber delivery density or a buying-group term changes the JIT-vs-shelf economics
a part class moves between fast-mover and slow-mover

nodes.definition: Set up the same-day jobber parts supply that anchors the mechanical sub-category (Nona's, Turlock Auto Service, E&M, plus Turlock Quick Smog & Repair): multiple same-day deliveries per day from NAPA, O'Reilly, and WORLDPAC plus the local Turlock Auto Parts counter for hot-shot pulls, OE dealer for special-order in 1-3 days, and possible program-group access. This is the JIT backbone that lets a mechanical shop hold minimal shelf stock beyond fast movers while keeping a bay turning, and it is the routing source for the parts line that runs ~30-40% of mechanical revenue.

included: same-day jobber routing and OE special-order lead time
the local Turlock Auto Parts hot-shot node
excluded: tire, paint, and rebuild-kit supply (own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: jobber delivery frequency, reach, or pricing changes

pros.claim: Multiple same-day jobber deliveries keep a bay turning on JIT parts without tying capital up in shelf inventory
pros.example: a mechanical shop pulling a brake or A/C part same-day from O'Reilly mid-job instead of stocking it

cons.claim: Same-day jobber reliance exposes the shop to a delivery gap or an OE special-order lead time that stalls a repair order
cons.example: an OE-only sensor on a 1-3 day special-order holding a car on the lift

failure_modes: single-sourcing one jobber so a delivery gap stops the line
stocking slow movers a same-day pull would have covered
acceptance_tests: the jobber routing names at least two same-day suppliers plus the OE special-order path and the local Turlock Auto Parts hot-shot option for the mechanical parts line
revisit_triggers: a jobber changes delivery frequency, reach, or pricing
OE special-order lead times shift materially

nodes.definition: Set up the inventory-carry model that defines the single independent parts retailer (Turlock Auto Parts, 'ASE parts specialists'): broad SKU depth held on the shelf and replenished daily/weekly from warehouse distributors, hot-shot delivery to shop trade accounts same day, and a counter-pro labor model serving DIY plus wholesale accounts. This is the opposite capital model from the JIT repair shops, the structural reason a town this size supports many service shops but only one independent parts store against AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA and online RockAuto/Amazon, surviving on counter expertise and trade accounts rather than retail price.

included: broad shelf-SKU depth and WD replenishment
trade-account hot-shot delivery and counter-pro labor

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: WD replenishment, buying-group terms, or trade-account demand changes

pros.claim: A trade-account and counter-expertise base lets the one independent parts store survive where retail price alone would lose to the nationals
pros.example: Turlock Auto Parts holding wholesale shop accounts and ASE counter pros rather than competing on shelf price with AutoZone

cons.claim: Broad shelf inventory ties up capital and carries obsolescence risk the JIT service shops never take on
cons.example: slow-moving SKUs aging on the shelf as online RockAuto undercuts the retail price

failure_modes: running an inventory-carry model without a wholesale trade-account base against the nationals
over-stocking slow SKUs that obsolesce before they sell
acceptance_tests: the parts-retail plan specifies shelf-SKU depth, WD replenishment cadence, and the trade-account/counter-pro base that differentiates it from the nationals
revisit_triggers: a warehouse distributor or buying-group term changes replenishment economics
trade-account demand or online competition shifts the inventory posture

nodes.definition: Set up the paint and panel supply for the collision sub-category (Broadway, Complete Collision Works): refinish paint from PPG or Axalta via PBE jobbers and LKQ Refinish, mixed on-site at a mixing bank, and panels from OE dealer, LKQ aftermarket/recycled (next-day), or Worldpac OE (days to 1-2 weeks, with back-order risk). Material flow is job-by-job after insurer approval, low SKU and JIT per repair order, with computerized paint matching (consistent with Complete Collision Works' on-site mixing). The supply cadence is paced by DRP approval, and the OE-panel back-order is the chief flow risk.

included: PPG/Axalta paint via LKQ Refinish and on-site mixing
LKQ aftermarket/recycled and Worldpac OE panel routing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a paint/panel supplier or DRP panel requirement changes

pros.claim: Routing paint via LKQ Refinish and panels across LKQ/Worldpac matches the JIT-after-approval flow collision actually runs
pros.example: a body shop pulling a next-day LKQ aftermarket panel while special-ordering the OE part that DRP requires

cons.claim: OE-panel lead times of days to 1-2 weeks create a back-order risk that stalls a repair order and ties up a stall
cons.example: a car occupying a frame stall for a week waiting on a back-ordered OE quarter panel

failure_modes: single-sourcing OE panels with no aftermarket/recycled fallback during a back-order
ordering paint or panels before insurer approval and carrying mismatched stock
acceptance_tests: paint is routed via PPG/Axalta and LKQ Refinish with on-site mixing, and panels across LKQ aftermarket/recycled and Worldpac OE with the back-order risk acknowledged
revisit_triggers: a paint or panel supplier changes price, availability, or lead time
a DRP insurer changes its OE-vs-aftermarket panel requirement

nodes.definition: Set up tire and wheel supply for the tires sub-category (Balswick's since 1945, Countryside, Mando's): same/next-day delivery from American Tire Distributors (the largest NA wholesaler, 90k+ SKUs) and NTW (Michelin/Sumitomo), plus direct from Michelin or Goodyear, holding fast movers and pulling odd sizes JIT from regional DCs. The structural reality is that tire-resale margin is thin and national chains and online (Tire Rack/SimpleTire ship-to-installer) own the commodity lane, so the supply plan exists to feed an attached-service model, not to win on tire-product margin.

included: fast-mover stock vs JIT odd-size pulls

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a tire wholesaler term or the tire-margin floor changes

pros.claim: Same/next-day ATD and NTW supply lets an independent stock only fast movers and pull odd sizes JIT
pros.example: a tire shop pulling an odd light-truck size next-day from an ATD regional DC instead of carrying it

cons.claim: Thin tire-resale margin means the supply chain alone cannot carry the shop without attached service
cons.example: an independent matching a Costco or online tire price and earning almost nothing on the tire itself

failure_modes: competing on tire-product price against chains and online with no service attach
over-stocking odd sizes a JIT next-day pull would have covered
acceptance_tests: tire supply is routed via ATD/NTW and direct-manufacturer with fast-mover stock and JIT odd-size pulls, and the thin-margin attached-service dependence is stated
revisit_triggers: a tire wholesaler changes delivery reach, SKU breadth, or pricing
online ship-to-installer competition shifts the local tire-margin floor

nodes.definition: Set up the rebuild-kit and drivetrain-parts supply for the transmission sub-category (Al's Transmissions, ATRA-affiliated; Turlock Transmissions): soft-parts, master, and super rebuild kits plus torque converters and valve bodies from Transtar (NexaMotion Group), with recycled units via Transend. Kits and converters ship per job, often 1-3 days, JIT per teardown, with some common kits stocked. This is a high-average-repair-order, low-volume specialty: margin lives in skilled drivetrain labor, the ATRA affiliation signals trade-standard rebuild practice and a warranty network, and the kit-ordering cadence is paced by teardown findings.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rebuild-kit supplier term or the transmission demand pool changes

pros.claim: Routing rebuild kits and converters through Transtar matches the JIT-per-teardown cadence the high-ARO specialty runs on
pros.example: ordering a master rebuild kit and converter only after teardown confirms the failure, holding minimal kit stock

cons.claim: Per-job kit ordering on a 1-3 day lead time stalls a teardown if no common kit is stocked
cons.example: a rebuild waiting days on a back-ordered valve body with the unit already torn down

failure_modes: holding no common-kit stock so every teardown waits on a 1-3 day kit
single-sourcing kits with no recycled-unit or second-supplier fallback
acceptance_tests: rebuild-kit and converter supply is routed via Transtar/NexaMotion with the Transend recycled option and a JIT-per-teardown cadence matched to the high-ARO low-volume reality
revisit_triggers: a rebuild-kit supplier changes price, availability, or lead time
the EV transition erodes the multi-speed-transmission demand pool

nodes.definition: Place the operator's sub-category on the deep-dive's capex ladder and name its capital anchor (all bands labeled estimates): mobile detailing rig $5k-$15k at the bottom, fixed detailing or per-bay mechanical tooling (lifts, scan tools, A/C machine, alignment) at mid-five-figures to $50k-$150k, the certified smog analyzer as concentrated single-instrument capex, tire mounting/balancing/road-force and alignment racks at moderate capex, transmission jacks/dyno/cleaning tanks as niche moderate capex, and the collision spray booth plus frame/measuring system at $50k-$150k+, the heaviest in the sector. Equipment depreciation and financing are heaviest for collision and smog.

included: the low-to-high capex ladder by sub-category
excluded: the smog analyzer and collision booth specifics (own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an equipment-capex band or the format's volume changes

pros.claim: Placing the format on the capex ladder up front sizes the capital anchor before a single tool is bought
pros.example: a startup detailer budgeting a $5k-$15k mobile rig rather than over-buying a fixed-shop bay it does not need

cons.claim: Treating the band as a point figure over- or under-states capex for a specific shop whose bay count is UNKNOWN
cons.example: quoting a flat collision capex when the $50k-$150k+ band is a wide labeled estimate

failure_modes: buying capital equipment mismatched to the format's volume
treating a wide labeled capex band as a precise figure
acceptance_tests: the sub-category is placed on the capex ladder with its capital anchor named and the band labeled an estimate, not a point figure
revisit_triggers: an equipment price or financing term shifts a capex band
the format's volume outgrows its current capital anchor

nodes.definition: Size the heaviest capex in the sector: the collision spray booth, frame/measuring system, paint mixing bank, welders, and PDR tools, commonly $50k-$150k+ (labeled estimate, wide range, low confidence). This booth-and-frame capital, together with the air-district VOC paint-booth permit and the DRP relationship gate, is the structural reason the local body-shop count is capped at two rather than reflecting a market gap. The capital anchor plus equipment financing make collision capital-intensive, and Complete Collision Works' 35+ years and computerized paint matching are the kind of equipment-and-longevity moat the gate rewards.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a booth/frame/paint-equipment price or an air-district/DRP requirement changes

pros.claim: Sizing the booth-and-frame capital up front shows collision's entry wall is capital and DRP, not accident volume
pros.example: a would-be body shop budgeting $50k-$150k+ for booth and frame and a DRP plan before counting on accident work

cons.claim: The capex band is a wide low-confidence estimate that can mislead if read as a precise entry figure
cons.example: treating $150k as the fixed cost when the band is a labeled estimate spanning setups

failure_modes: financing booth/frame capital without a DRP plan to fill it
reading the wide capex band as a precise number
acceptance_tests: the booth/frame capital anchor is named with the $50k-$150k+ band labeled an estimate and the capex-plus-DRP count-cap mechanism stated
revisit_triggers: a booth, frame, or paint-equipment price changes
an air-district VOC or DRP requirement changes the collision capital picture

nodes.definition: Choose the labor model that fits the sub-category. Owner-operator/family-run dominates this catalog (Broadway family-owned, E&M family since 2012, Nona's 40+ years, Mando's family-owned, Balswick's since 1945) and structurally suppresses the published labor-cost benchmark, the same lever the food sector uses. W-2 technician crews staff repair, collision, and transmission, where labor is the revenue engine (labor rate x billed hours) and technician productivity (billed vs paid hours) is the lever. Booth/chair-rental is not typical here; the low-barrier analog is the solo-operator/mobile detailer who can shed occupancy cost entirely. The Spanish-language and heritage referral channel lowers customer-acquisition cost.

included: owner-operator/family-run, W-2 crew, and solo-mobile models
billed-vs-paid technician productivity as the lever

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the labor model, crew size, or productivity lever changes

pros.claim: Matching the labor model to the sub-category sets the right cost structure and productivity lever
pros.example: a multi-bay mechanical shop staffing a W-2 crew and managing billed-vs-paid hours as its margin lever

cons.claim: Family-labor suppression of the benchmark can hide the true cost when the owner-operator scales to a hired crew
cons.example: a family shop adding W-2 techs and discovering the suppressed labor benchmark no longer holds

failure_modes: assuming a booth/chair-rental model that is not typical in this sector
ignoring billed-vs-paid productivity as the core repair-labor lever
acceptance_tests: the labor model is selected as owner-operator/family, W-2 crew, or solo-mobile with the productivity lever and referral-channel edge named for the sub-category
revisit_triggers: the shop scales from owner-operator to a hired crew
the labor mix or productivity lever materially shifts

nodes.definition: Treat credential-gated labor as a hiring bottleneck, not just a cost line. Licensed smog inspectors (a separate BAR license, ~$20 app and ~$20 renewal per 2 years) and, for DRP collision work, I-CAR Gold Class / ASE technicians are credential-constrained labor whose scarcity caps how fast a smog station or DRP body shop can scale. These are private credentials (I-CAR/ASE) or state licenses (smog inspector) that gate the labor supply itself: a station cannot inspect without a licensed inspector on shift, and a body shop cannot win DRP work without certified techs, so the credential is both a hiring constraint and a moat once cleared.

included: licensed smog inspector and I-CAR/ASE collision tech constraints
credential scarcity as a scaling cap
the credential as both bottleneck and moat

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a credential requirement or the local credentialed-labor supply changes

pros.claim: Naming credential-gated labor as a bottleneck lets the operator plan hiring around the constraint that actually caps scale
pros.example: a smog station planning a backup licensed inspector before it staffs a second bay it could not legally run otherwise

cons.claim: Over-weighting the credential constraint can deter entry into a gated lane whose credential is also its moat
cons.example: an operator avoiding the smog lane over the inspector license when the license is precisely what keeps the lane defensible

failure_modes: staffing a smog or DRP bay with no credentialed technician available
treating the credential as a cost line rather than a hard scaling cap
acceptance_tests: the credential-gated roles (licensed smog inspector, I-CAR/ASE collision tech) are identified as scaling constraints with the credential noted as both bottleneck and moat
revisit_triggers: a BAR inspector-license or I-CAR/ASE requirement changes
the credentialed-labor supply tightens or loosens locally

nodes.definition: Set up the smog/inspection sub-category's licensing fork (All Valley Smog test-and-repair, Speed Pass Smog test-only, Turlock Quick Smog & Repair smog plus repair): the BAR station license (test-and-repair / test-only / repair-only), the separately licensed smog inspector, and voluntary STAR certification that lets a station inspect DMV-directed vehicles with no application/renewal fee but requiring performance standards plus a current ARD and station license. The state-set $8.25 certificate fee is the only regulated dollar figure; the $30-$80 per-test price is an unregulated market estimate. Losing STAR removes directed-vehicle volume, making it a recurring-demand gate.

included: station license fork, inspector license, STAR certification

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a station/inspector/STAR rule, the $8.25 fee, or the smog-eligible pool changes

pros.claim: Clearing the station/inspector/STAR fork unlocks the recurring, inelastic, directed-vehicle smog demand the deep-dive calls most defensible
pros.example: a STAR test-and-repair station capturing DMV-directed vehicles a non-STAR station cannot inspect

cons.claim: STAR performance standards and a licensed inspector are a real entry wall that a test-only lean operator must still clear
cons.example: a station losing STAR over a performance standard and with it its directed-vehicle volume

failure_modes: advertising directed-vehicle inspections without STAR standing
quoting the $30-$80 test price as a regulated fact like the $8.25 fee
acceptance_tests: the station license, inspector license, and STAR requirements are stated with the $8.25 regulated fee distinguished from the $30-$80 market-estimate test price
revisit_triggers: a BAR station/inspector or STAR rule or fee changes
the EV transition erodes the smog-eligible vehicle pool

nodes.definition: Establish the DRP relationship gate that is the binding constraint on the collision sub-category (Broadway, Complete Collision Works). Direct Repair Program relationships drive roughly 90% of collision revenue (~82% of insured nationally use a DRP shop, a 2020 national figure that may not reflect 2026 Turlock), so a new body shop's viability hinges on landing insurer DRP relationships, not on finding accident volume. Whether a specific named shop holds particular DRP contracts is UNKNOWN. DRP is gatekept by I-CAR/ASE certification and equipment, structurally capping the local count at two and leaking high-ticket complex jobs north to Modesto consolidators.

included: DRP as the binding collision constraint

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an insurer DRP term or the local collision DRP landscape changes

pros.claim: Naming DRP as the binding constraint reframes collision entry around insurer relationships rather than accident volume
pros.example: a body shop prioritizing landing a DRP relationship over advertising for walk-in collision work

cons.claim: The 90%-DRP figure is a 2020 national datapoint that may overstate Turlock's 2026 DRP dependence
cons.example: assuming the national DRP share applies unchanged to a small independent local body shop

failure_modes: financing a body shop with no DRP plan and relying on walk-in accident volume
stating a specific shop's DRP contract as fact when it is UNKNOWN
acceptance_tests: DRP is stated as the binding collision constraint with the ~90%-of-revenue figure labeled a 2020 national estimate and specific-shop contracts tagged UNKNOWN
revisit_triggers: an insurer changes its DRP terms or panel requirements
the local DRP landscape or Modesto leakage shifts

nodes.definition: Set up the service-attach model that is the survival mechanism in the commodity lanes. Standalone tire resale loses to chains and online; tire plus alignment plus brake plus general mechanical wins, and the independents that survive are mini-integrated (E&M sells parts and tires; Balswick's does tires plus repair plus detail; Countryside does tire plus brake; Mando's does tire/wheel plus repair). The same logic extends mechanical attach onto smog (Turlock Quick Smog & Repair captures fail-then-repair revenue). The node defines which higher-margin services to bundle onto the commodity transaction so the shop earns on attached labor rather than thin product margin.

included: bundling alignment/brake/mechanical onto tire and smog transactions
earning on attached labor not product margin

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the commodity-margin floor or the shop's attach capability changes

pros.claim: Attaching higher-margin service onto a commodity transaction is how an independent survives a lane the chains own
pros.example: a tire shop earning on the alignment and brake job attached to a thin-margin tire sale

cons.claim: Service attach demands the broader BAR-licensed capability and tooling a pure-product seller avoids
cons.example: a tire shop needing ARD registration and alignment/brake tooling to capture the attach it depends on

failure_modes: selling commodity tires with no attached service against chain and online pricing
attaching services the shop lacks the license or tooling to perform
acceptance_tests: the higher-margin attach services are named for the tire (and smog) transaction with the mini-integrated survivor pattern stated
revisit_triggers: the commodity-product margin floor or chain/online competition shifts
the shop gains or loses the license/tooling for an attach service

nodes.definition: Model revenue and margin as a labeled benchmark estimate and never as a named business's actual figure. Method: take a published national per-unit benchmark (~$203k revenue/bay PartsTech mechanical, independent tire store $500k-$2M, profitable smog station $180k-$450k/yr, ~$1.2M average collision shop, transmission $250k-$500k/bay, ~$250k average detailing establishment) times an inferred size signal (bay count read from the offering, years in business, mobile-vs-shop, DRP language, all UNKNOWN for named firms) times the sub-category band, then tag the result estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and state the confirmation path (operator records or CDTFA receipts). Central Valley rates run modestly below coastal CA, so true figures sit at the lower-middle of each band.

included: the benchmark x inferred-size-signal x band method

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published benchmark updates or actual financial data becomes available

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark method yields a usable revenue estimate without ever asserting a private firm's actual figures
pros.example: estimating a mechanical shop's revenue as ~$203k/bay x an inferred 3-8 bays, tagged medium-confidence with a records confirmation path

cons.claim: Wide bands times UNKNOWN size signals carry real uncertainty that misleads if the estimate label is dropped downstream
cons.example: a planning estimate later quoted as a measured revenue for a named shop

failure_modes: stating a per-business dollar figure as fact instead of a labeled estimate
using a sub-category mean as if it were a typical specific business
acceptance_tests: every revenue/margin figure is derived as benchmark x inferred size signal x band, tagged estimate-not-actual with confidence and a named confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark updates
actual operator records or CDTFA data become available to replace an estimate

nodes.definition: Assemble the consolidated operating-model plan that turns the scattered supply, capex, labor, and licensing decisions into one operating system: the inventory posture and named primary/backup suppliers per input class, the capex ladder placement and capital anchor, the labor model and credential constraints, the licensing gates cleared, the service-attach bundle, and the labeled revenue/margin estimates. It is the single artifact an operator works from to set up the shop and run weekly operations, with every dollar figure carrying its estimate label and every supplier link tagged verified or inference.

included: primary/backup per input with capex and labor anchors
excluded: individual node decisions already made upstream

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a supplier, capex, labor, or licensing element of the plan changes

pros.claim: One consolidated plan converts a pile of operating decisions into an executable setup-and-weekly-operations system with no orphaned input
pros.example: a single sheet listing every input class, its supplier, the capex anchor, the labor model, and the cleared licenses

cons.claim: A fixed plan can ossify and miss a better mid-stream supplier or capex opportunity without a review loop
cons.example: sticking to a jobber line when a buying-group rebate would beat it, absent the review loop

failure_modes: a plan with an input class that has no assigned supplier or backup
compliance and honesty hooks (licenses, estimate labels) left off the plan
acceptance_tests: the plan lists every input class with a primary supplier, a backup, a capex anchor, a labor model, the cleared licenses, and labeled-estimate cost hooks
revisit_triggers: a supplier, capex, labor, or licensing element of the plan changes
the review loop flags a better operating path

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the operating-model plan alive: a fixed price-and-availability review cadence (a monthly jobber/tire price-list check plus a quarterly full supply-capex-labor review) and the material-change triggers, a parts or tire price spike, a lost or merged supplier, a BAR/STAR or air-district rule change, an analyzer or booth equipment failure, a credential-labor shortage, a sub-category or service-mix change, or the EV transition eroding a smog/transmission pool, that send the operator back through SUBCATEGORY_COST_PROFILE and the supply nodes to re-plan. Without this loop the plan silently drifts out of cost, compliance, and resilience alignment.

included: re-entry into cost profile and supply nodes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

pros.claim: A scheduled review catches price drift, supplier risk, and rule changes before they compress the thin net margin for months
pros.example: a quarterly review spotting a jobber line now beaten by a buying-group rebate and rerouting it

cons.claim: Reviewing too often churns supplier relationships and prevents any volume break or rebate from maturing
cons.example: re-tendering every parts line monthly so no jobber grants a loyalty price

failure_modes: no cadence set so the plan is never revisited and drifts
ignoring a material-change trigger and running a now-misaligned plan
acceptance_tests: a review cadence and an explicit list of material-change triggers exist, each routing back to SUBCATEGORY_COST_PROFILE and the relevant supply nodes
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse

edges.why_related: the parc demand read bounds which sub-category cost centers are essential and must be profiled
the named-firm catalog grounds the cost profile in real cross-categorized sub-categories
the supplier universe is matched against the named firms in the catalog
the dominant cost center decides whether parts are consumed JIT or carried on the shelf
jobber delivery density in the supplier universe determines the viable inventory posture
the JIT posture sets up the same-day jobber routing for the mechanical parts line
the shelf-carry posture defines the parts-retail inventory model
the collision paint-and-panel cost center defines the paint/panel sourcing need
the paint/panel segment of the supplier universe routes PPG/Axalta and LKQ/Worldpac
the tire COGS-and-attach cost center defines the tire sourcing need
the tire-wholesaler segment of the supplier universe routes ATD/NTW and direct-manufacturer
the rebuild-kit-and-skilled-labor cost center defines the transmission kit sourcing need
the rebuild-kit segment of the supplier universe routes Transtar/NexaMotion and Transend
the cost profile and production needs determine the format's capital anchor on the capex ladder
licensing gates (air-district booth permit, certified analyzer) shape required capital equipment
the collision booth and frame are the heaviest rung of the capex ladder
on-site paint mixing and panel work require the booth and frame capital to be in place
the labor-driven cost profile of repair/collision/transmission selects the labor model
the labor-model choice surfaces which credential-gated roles bottleneck scaling
the smog-inspector license and DRP credential gates come from the regulatory regime
the smog station/STAR licensing fork is a specialization of the regulatory gate set
the de-facto I-CAR/ASE and air-district gates set the collision DRP entry conditions
DRP work requires the I-CAR/ASE credential-gated technicians the labor node identifies
the thin-product-margin cost profile of tires/smog drives the service-attach decision
the thin tire-supply margin is the reason the shop must attach higher-margin service
the honesty charter sets the never-state-actuals rule the benchmark method implements
the revenue estimate is built per sub-category from the cost profile and its benchmark band
the jobber parts routing is a core line of the consolidated operating plan
the capex placement and capital anchor are core lines of the consolidated operating plan
the labeled revenue/margin estimate is a required hook in the consolidated plan
the review loop watches the consolidated plan and triggers re-planning
a sub-category or service-mix change sends the operator back to re-profile the cost center
the JIT same-day jobber model and the shelf-inventory-carry model are opposite capital strategies competing for the same parts spend
edges.resolution_rule: run JIT same-day jobber sourcing for a repair shop that consumes parts per job; commit to shelf-inventory carry only for a parts retailer with a wholesale trade-account base that can absorb the carrying cost

edges.why_related: investing in attached-service capability competes for capital and focus against scaling thin-margin tire-product volume
edges.resolution_rule: treat tire product as a loss-leading traffic driver and put capital into the alignment/brake/mechanical attach where the margin actually is, rather than chasing tire-product volume against the chains

edges.why_related: heavy booth/frame capital and the DRP relationship gate must both be cleared, and committing capex before landing DRP risks stranded capital
edges.resolution_rule: secure a credible DRP relationship pathway before financing the full $50k-$150k+ booth/frame capital, so the capital-intensive collision setup is filled by insurer-referred volume rather than stranded on walk-in work

edges.why_related: the service-attach bundle is a core line of the consolidated operating plan

conflict_axes.name: jit_per_job_vs_shelf_inventory_carry
conflict_axes.description: Ordering parts JIT per repair order keeps capital in equipment and labor, while carrying broad shelf inventory serves off-the-shelf retail but ties up capital and takes obsolescence risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: JIT for repair shops that consume parts per job; shelf carry only for a parts retailer with a wholesale trade-account base

conflict_axes.name: tire_product_volume_vs_service_attach
conflict_axes.description: Chasing thin-margin tire-product volume against chains and online competes with investing in the attached alignment/brake/mechanical service where the real margin sits.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat tire product as a traffic driver and put capital into the higher-margin attach

conflict_axes.name: capex_first_vs_gate_first
conflict_axes.description: Financing heavy booth/frame or analyzer capital before clearing the DRP or STAR/licensing gate risks stranded capital, but waiting on the gate can delay the equipment a gated lane requires.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: secure the DRP/STAR/license pathway before committing the heaviest sub-category capex

conflict_axes.name: owner_operator_labor_vs_w2_crew
conflict_axes.description: Owner-operator/family labor suppresses the labor benchmark and sheds occupancy for mobile, but caps capacity, while a W-2 crew scales output at the published labor cost and the billed-vs-paid productivity risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run owner-operator/mobile at low volume; add a W-2 crew only when billable demand clears the published labor cost

conflict_axes.name: single_supplier_simplicity_vs_resilience
conflict_axes.description: Consolidating spend with one jobber, tire wholesaler, or kit supplier simplifies ordering and earns volume breaks but concentrates outage and lead-time risk on the dominant input.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: single-source low-risk commodities for the break; always keep a qualified second source for the dominant cost-center input

conflict_axes.name: buying_group_commitment_vs_price_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Committing to a buying group earns member rebates and WD access but locks spend to its lines and dulls the leverage of shopping a competing distributor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: join a group for the rebate floor on core lines but keep an outside-distributor option for one-off competitive prices

conflict_axes.name: oe_part_correctness_vs_aftermarket_cost_speed
conflict_axes.description: OE panels and parts satisfy DRP and fit requirements but carry days-to-weeks lead time and higher cost, while aftermarket/recycled is faster and cheaper but may not meet the insurer spec.
poles: source aftermarket/recycled for cost and speed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use aftermarket/recycled where the DRP spec allows and reserve OE special-order for parts the insurer requires

conflict_axes.name: test_only_lean_vs_test_and_repair_breadth
conflict_axes.description: A test-only smog station runs the leanest capex and simplest license but captures only inspection revenue, while test-and-repair captures fail-then-repair value at more tooling, ARD scope, and labor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: start test-only for the lean capex and add repair scope only when fail-then-repair volume justifies the tooling and labor

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_rigor_vs_point_figure_clarity
conflict_axes.description: Labeling every dollar figure a benchmark estimate with method and confidence protects honesty but reads as hedging to a planner who wants a single clean point figure.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always label the estimate with its band and confidence; never collapse it to an unqualified point figure for a named business

edge_cases.description: A repair shop runs an inventory-carry model against the national jobbers with no wholesale trade-account base
edge_cases.trigger: an independent stocks broad shelf SKUs to compete on retail price with AutoZone/O'Reilly
edge_cases.mitigation: run JIT same-day jobber sourcing for a service shop, and reserve shelf carry for a parts retailer with a wholesale trade base

edge_cases.description: A body shop finances the booth and frame capital before landing any DRP relationship
edge_cases.trigger: a collision startup commits $50k-$150k+ capex relying on walk-in accident volume
edge_cases.mitigation: secure a credible DRP pathway before committing the heavy booth/frame capital so insurer-referred volume fills it

edge_cases.description: A smog station advertises DMV-directed inspections without current STAR standing
edge_cases.trigger: a station markets directed-vehicle work after losing or before earning STAR
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm STAR standing, station license, and a licensed inspector on shift before advertising directed-vehicle inspections

edge_cases.description: An OE panel back-order of days to weeks strands a car in a frame stall with no aftermarket fallback
edge_cases.trigger: a DRP-required OE panel is single-sourced and back-ordered
edge_cases.mitigation: use an LKQ aftermarket/recycled panel where the DRP spec allows and pre-clear the OE-vs-aftermarket requirement

edge_cases.description: A transmission rebuild stalls because no common kit is stocked and a kit is on a 1-3 day back-order
edge_cases.trigger: a teardown finds a failure whose kit is not on hand and is back-ordered
edge_cases.mitigation: stock the common master/soft-parts kits and qualify Transend recycled units as a fallback for the dominant failures

edge_cases.description: The dominant cost-center input is single-sourced and the supplier stocks out mid-job
edge_cases.trigger: the only jobber, tire wholesaler, or kit supplier for the main input runs short with no backup
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-qualify a second source for the dominant cost-center input and route to it on the substitution rule

edge_cases.description: A tire shop competes on tire-product price against chains and online with no attached service
edge_cases.trigger: an independent matches a Costco/online tire price and earns nothing on the product
edge_cases.mitigation: treat tire product as a traffic driver and earn on the attached alignment/brake/mechanical service

edge_cases.description: A smog or DRP bay is staffed with no credentialed inspector or I-CAR/ASE technician available
edge_cases.trigger: a credential-gated role is unfilled when the bay needs to run
edge_cases.mitigation: qualify a backup licensed inspector or certified technician before relying on a single credentialed staffer

edge_cases.description: A per-business dollar figure is stated as fact instead of a labeled benchmark estimate
edge_cases.trigger: a revenue, margin, or capex number for a named shop is quoted without the estimate-not-actual label
edge_cases.mitigation: derive every figure as benchmark x inferred size signal x band, tag it estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

edge_cases.description: The $30-$80 smog test price is presented as a regulated fact like the $8.25 certificate fee
edge_cases.trigger: the unregulated market test price is quoted as a regulated figure
edge_cases.mitigation: state only the $8.25 certificate fee as regulated and label the $30-$80 test price an unregulated market estimate

edge_cases.description: The EV transition erodes the smog-eligible and multi-speed-transmission demand pools
edge_cases.trigger: local BEV adoption removes smog-eligible vehicles and multi-speed transmissions
edge_cases.mitigation: track the local EV timeline as a directional headwind offset by the ag-fleet/older-parc tailwind and re-run the demand read

workflow.gate: the parc estimate and aging/ag-fleet skew are stated with the essential sub-categories

workflow.description: List the 19 cataloged independents by sub-category with cross-categorization noted
workflow.gate: the 19 firms are listed by sub-category as a coverage floor not a ceiling

workflow.description: List the BAR ARD, CDTFA, smog/STAR, air-district VOC, hazmat, and city-license gates by sub-category
workflow.gate: the relevant gates are documented with the sub-categories each binds before any work is taken in

workflow.gate: the dominant cost center is named and at least three more cost lines are ranked

workflow.description: Enumerate channel-segmented suppliers verified to serve Turlock and tag inference vs verified
workflow.gate: six+ channel segments each have a named geography-verified provider

workflow.description: Choose JIT per-repair-order versus shelf-carry per part class with the capital-model rationale

workflow.description: Route jobber, collision paint/panel, tire, transmission kit, and detailing chemical supply to named providers
workflow.gate: every input class is routed to a named or representative supplier

workflow.action: Size the capex equipment ladder and capital anchor
workflow.description: Place the format on the capex ladder and name the capital anchor with labeled-estimate bands
workflow.gate: the sub-category is placed on the ladder with its capital anchor named and bands labeled estimates

workflow.action: Select the labor model and credential constraints
workflow.description: Choose owner-operator/family, W-2 crew, or solo-mobile and flag credential-gated roles
workflow.gate: the labor model is selected with the productivity lever and any credential bottleneck named

workflow.action: Build labeled revenue, margin, and capex estimates
workflow.description: Derive figures as benchmark x inferred size signal x band, tagged estimate-not-actual
workflow.gate: every dollar figure is labeled estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

workflow.action: Assemble the consolidated operating-model plan and review loop
workflow.description: Integrate supply, capex, labor, licensing, attach, and cost hooks, then set the review cadence and triggers
workflow.gate: every input class has a supplier, backup, capex anchor, labor model, cleared licenses, and labeled-cost hook, with a review cadence and triggers set

priority_rationale: Foundational demand-parc, business-catalog, licensing-gate, and honesty-charter work units precede everything because every operating choice depends on the parc-keyed demand, the named-firm catalog, the legal preconditions, and the labeling discipline; the cost-profile, supplier-universe, and inventory nodes set the operating spine; the sub-category supply, capex, labor, and licensing nodes build the format-specific operating model; the honesty and consolidated-plan nodes compose those into a hardened, honestly-costed system; and the review loop comes last because it watches the whole plan and routes material changes back to the foundations.

dominance_rules.rule: Licensing-gate readiness dominates any operating setup order
dominance_rules.rationale: no shop can legally take in work for compensation without its BAR ARD and any sub-category station/technician license, and no body shop wins DRP work without certified techs
dominance_rules.trigger: any plan to take in work or place a first supplier order
dominance_rules.action: block operations until the ARD and relevant sub-category licenses are in place

dominance_rules.rule: A DRP pathway dominates heavy collision capex commitment
dominance_rules.rationale: booth/frame capital with no DRP relationship is stranded capital, since ~90% of collision revenue is DRP-driven
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan to finance the booth/frame before a DRP pathway exists
dominance_rules.action: secure a credible DRP relationship pathway before committing the $50k-$150k+ capex

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labeling dominates any revenue, margin, or capex figure
dominance_rules.rationale: a per-business dollar number stated as fact violates the financial-honesty charter and misleads planning
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure about a named business or its operations
dominance_rules.action: express it only as a labeled benchmark estimate with method, source, and confidence

dominance_rules.rule: The regulated $8.25 fee dominates the market test-price figure
dominance_rules.rationale: conflating the unregulated $30-$80 test price with the regulated $8.25 certificate fee misstates what is actually regulated
dominance_rules.trigger: a smog price is presented as a regulated fact
dominance_rules.action: state only the $8.25 certificate fee as regulated and label the test price a market estimate

dominance_rules.rule: A backup for the dominant cost-center input dominates volume-discount consolidation
dominance_rules.rationale: an outage on the format's main input (parts, paint, tire, or kit) stops service, costing more than the consolidation discount earns
dominance_rules.trigger: the dominant cost-center input is about to be single-sourced
dominance_rules.action: qualify a second source before consolidating the rest

dominance_rules.rule: Service attach dominates competing on commodity tire-product price
dominance_rules.rationale: standalone tire resale loses to chains and online, while attached alignment/brake/mechanical is where the margin is
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan to win on tire-product price against the chains
dominance_rules.action: treat tire product as a traffic driver and earn on the attached service

dominance_rules.rule: The sub-category cost profile dominates generic supply defaults
dominance_rules.rationale: the right supplier, capex, and labor follow from which cost center dominates, not from a one-size default
dominance_rules.trigger: a supply or capex decision made before the cost center is profiled
dominance_rules.action: profile the dominant cost center first, then choose supply and capex around it

dominance_rules.rule: Credential-gated labor availability dominates a bay's scaling plan
dominance_rules.rationale: a smog or DRP bay cannot legally or competitively run without its credentialed staffer, so the credential caps scale
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan to add a smog or DRP bay without a credentialed staffer confirmed
dominance_rules.action: secure a licensed inspector or certified technician before committing the bay

dominance_rules.rule: The review loop dominates impulse supplier switches
dominance_rules.rationale: structured review prevents churning a maturing jobber or buying-group relationship over a transient price wiggle
dominance_rules.trigger: a tempting one-off price appears mid-cycle
dominance_rules.action: evaluate it through the review loop, not on impulse

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear the BAR ARD and sub-category licensing gate before taking in work or sourcing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: performing tests/repairs for compensation a shop is not yet licensed to perform

anti_rework_rules.rule: Profile the dominant cost center before choosing suppliers, capex, and labor
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a supply and capex setup around the wrong cost line and re-sourcing later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Secure a DRP pathway before financing the booth and frame capital
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stranding heavy collision capital with no insurer-referred volume to fill it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify a backup for every dominant cost-center input before single-sourcing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a service-stopping outage with no substitute ready when the primary parts/paint/tire/kit source fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a supplier actually delivers to Turlock before building it into the plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing the plan around a vendor whose reach or minimums exclude the county

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm a credentialed inspector or certified technician before committing a gated bay
anti_rework_rules.prevents: standing up a smog or DRP bay that cannot legally or competitively run

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every revenue, margin, and capex figure estimate-not-actual when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a planning estimate being quoted downstream as a measured per-business fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Match the inventory posture to whether parts are consumed per job or sold off the shelf
anti_rework_rules.prevents: carrying obsolescent shelf stock in a JIT shop or starving a retail counter of depth

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every supplier-to-named-business link verified or inference before relying on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: treating a representative supplier inference as a confirmed contract and planning around a link that does not exist

iteration_protocol.trigger: the operator changes or adds a sub-category or service line
iteration_protocol.action: re-profile the dominant cost center and re-run supply, capex, and labor

iteration_protocol.trigger: a tracked parts, paint, tire, or kit price spikes
iteration_protocol.action: trigger substitution and re-run the cost estimate and supply routing

iteration_protocol.trigger: a primary supplier is lost, merges, or stocks out
iteration_protocol.action: activate the backup, re-qualify the channel, and update the plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a BAR ARD, smog/STAR, air-district, or DRP licensing rule changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-clear the affected gate and adjust the licensing and labor plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a credentialed inspector or certified technician becomes unavailable
iteration_protocol.action: activate the credentialed-labor backup and re-plan the affected bay

iteration_protocol.trigger: an analyzer, booth, or major tool fails or the format outgrows it
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the capex anchor and adjust the operating plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: the EV transition measurably erodes the smog or transmission demand pool
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the parc demand read and reassess the affected sub-category supply

iteration_protocol.trigger: a published benchmark updates or actual records become available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the affected labeled estimate and re-derive the figures
